name: Alyeska Resort downhill skiing
hoursOrDates: Lifts open daily (day hours ~10:30-dusk, unverified). Night skiing runs every day 18 Dec 2026 - 3 Jan 2027 until 8pm. 31 Dec: mountain closes at 5pm.
cost: Adult day ticket ~$119-169, holiday pricing (third-party figure); $49 night tickets are Jan-Mar only
notes: Alaska's biggest ski area, with 2,500 ft of vertical straight above tidewater and Turnagain Arm views. Holiday week is peak: buy online ahead and expect crowds. Lit night skiing helps with ~5.5 h of daylight. Upper mountain often goes on wind or visibility holds. Seward Hwy avalanche closures can block access.

name: Alyeska Aerial Tram (sightseeing) + Seven Glaciers
hoursOrDates: Winter daily 11:30am-6pm, until 8pm on night-ski days (which is every day 18 Dec - 3 Jan). Holiday-day hours not published.
cost: Foot-passenger winter ticket ? (summer $55 adult); Seven Glaciers dinner $$$$
notes: A 4-min ride to 2,300 ft, with views of 7 glaciers and Turnagain Arm. Ride up before sunset (~15:45) for alpenglow. Seven Glaciers fine dining at the top needs a reservation; in summer that includes a free tram ride, so ask whether it does in winter. Closes in high wind.

name: Girdwood village
hoursOrDates: Year-round
notes: A ski-town base with cafes and brewery. Gets far more snow than Anchorage. Pairs with AWCC, Portage and the Nordic spa on a single Turnagain Arm day.

name: Flattop Mountain / Glen Alps (winter hike & snowshoe)
hoursOrDates: Year-round, daylight
notes: Anchorage's classic hike: 3 mi round trip, ~1,350 ft gain, city/Cook Inlet/Denali views. Winter summit gully is icy and avalanche-prone, with past fatalities. Most groups should stop at Blueberry Knoll or the saddle, or snowshoe the gentler Powerline Pass valley, and carry microspikes. Check the CNFAIC forecast. Glen Alps Rd is steep and icy. Lot fills on clear days.

name: Thunderbird Falls
hoursOrDates: Year-round, daylight
notes: Easy ~2 mi round trip to a 200-ft falls that often freezes into ice sculpture. Trail is packed and icy, so microspikes are essential. The side trail down to the creek is steep and slick. Good short outing or add-on to Eklutna Lake.

name: Eklutna Lake (Lakeside Trail)
hoursOrDates: Year-round, daylight
notes: Big frozen glacial lake ringed by peaks. The Lakeside Trail is flat (out-and-back any distance) and good for walking, snowshoeing or fat-biking. The 10-mile Eklutna Lake Rd is winding and icy. Very windy and cold at the lake, and the side valleys are avalanche terrain. Ice on the lake is unmonitored. Good aurora spot if clear.

name: Portage Lake & Portage Glacier (walk on frozen lake)
hoursOrDates: Year-round road access, daylight. Lake crossing only once ice is solid, which is often not yet safe in late Dec.
notes: In a good ice year you can walk ~3 mi each way across the lake to the blue face of Portage Glacier. The ice is NOT monitored, sits over a 600-ft-deep lake, and changes day to day. Ask the Glacier Ranger District (907-783-3242) for ice reports, carry ice picks, and stay well back from the calving face. Otherwise enjoy the view from the shore and parking area. Valley can be very windy.

name: Begich, Boggs Visitor Center
hoursOrDates: CLOSED in winter (open Memorial Day - Labor Day, Thu-Sun 9-5). Not open 23 Dec - 3 Jan.
notes: Building closed for winter. The shoreline/parking area is still a scenic stop.

name: Byron Glacier Trail
hoursOrDates: Year-round, but the Forest Service advises against winter travel
notes: Flat ~1.4 mi to a glacier view, but the trail runs through avalanche runout under steep valley walls. Both the Forest Service and CNFAIC say avoid it in winter unless you have avalanche gear and training. Trailhead road may be unplowed, adding ~0.5 mi on foot. Never enter the 'ice caves', which are avalanche debris that collapses.

name: Alaska Wildlife Conservation Center
hoursOrDates: Dec/Jan: Fri-Mon 10am-4pm (last entry 3pm), plus special holiday days 22, 23, 29, 30, 31 Dec 2026. CLOSED 24 Dec, 25 Dec, 1 Jan. In the trip window it is open 23, 26-31 Dec and 2-3 Jan.
notes: Rescue sanctuary with wood bison, musk ox, moose, elk, caribou, wolves, lynx and bears (bears may be denned). Walk or drive the 1.5-mi loop. Cold and windy in Portage Valley. Combine with Girdwood and Portage. Buy tickets online.

name: Beluga Point (Seward Hwy Mile 110)
hoursOrDates: Year-round pullout
notes: Rocky point with big Turnagain Arm and Kenai Mountains views. Ice floes and hoarfrost in winter, and belugas are unlikely then. Dall sheep are often seen on the cliffs at Windy Point (~Mile 106, coords not verified) a few minutes south. Decent aurora spot. Seward Hwy: high-wind, icy, avalanche-closure-prone stretch with lots of head-on crashes, so drive in daylight with headlights on.

name: Bird Point Scenic Overlook (Seward Hwy Mile 96)
hoursOrDates: Year-round, daylight
notes: Overlook and short paths at the head of the Arm, by the Bird-to-Gird pathway. Winter views of ice-choked Turnagain Arm. Notoriously windy. Between Indian and Girdwood the Seward Hwy has avalanche paths and DOT control closures.

name: Potter Marsh boardwalk
hoursOrDates: Year-round
notes: Boardwalk over a wetland refuge. In winter it is frozen and quiet, with few birds but occasional moose and good low-sun photos. A quick first stop on any Turnagain Arm drive. Boardwalk can be icy or snow-covered.

name: Matanuska Glacier winter guided walk
coordNote: Matanuska Glacier Park lodge/gate (66500 S Glacier Park Rd)
hoursOrDates: Winter daily departures 10am, 11am, 1pm, 2pm (weather permitting). Arrive 1 h early. Holiday-day operation ?
cost: ~$150-160 pp incl. guide, crampons/spikes and gate; full-day tours from Anchorage ~$310-375
notes: Walk on a huge road-accessible valley glacier with blue ice and seasonal ice caves. In winter you may only go on the ice with a guide, and operators sometimes use a snowmachine sled for the approach. 4 h round-trip drive on the winding, icy Glenn Hwy (Sheep Mountain, Caribou Creek), so leave Anchorage by ~8am to use daylight. Often -10 to -20F with strong Matanuska/Knik winds near Palmer.

name: Hatcher Pass & Independence Mine SHP
hoursOrDates: Road usually plowed to the Independence Mine area. Summit road closed to cars in winter. Mine visitor center closed in winter. Closures after storms and avalanches.
notes: Alpine bowl with historic gold-mine buildings, snowshoeing, sledding and huge views. Lodge (open year-round, hours ?) serves food. Steep avalanche terrain everywhere off-road: check the Hatcher Pass Avalanche Center (hpavalanche.org) and 511.alaska.gov. Colder and windier than Anchorage, and the upper road can be icy, so snow tires are needed. Dark-sky aurora option.

name: Alaska Railroad Aurora Winter Train
hoursOrDates: Weekends only in the window. Northbound Sat 26 Dec and Sat 2 Jan: Anc 8:30am, Wasilla 9:50, Talkeetna 11:25, Fairbanks 8:00pm. Southbound Sun 27 Dec and Sun 3 Jan: Fairbanks 8:30am, Talkeetna 4:50pm, Wasilla 6:25, Anc 8:00pm. No extra holiday-week runs are listed for 2026-27, and midweek runs are Feb-Mar only.
cost: Anc-Fairbanks ~$265 one way adult (2026-27, secondary source); Anc-Talkeetna ?
notes: Scenic winter rail through Susitna Valley backcountry, with Denali views if clear and only ~5.5 h of daylight. Talkeetna by train has to be an overnight (Sat up, Sun back). A same-day round trip is not possible. Adventure Class only. Book early for holiday weekends. Times vary with flagstops and the train can run late.

name: Talkeetna
hoursOrDates: Year-round town. Many shops and restaurants close or cut hours in winter.
notes: Funky end-of-road town with Denali views on clear days from the riverside overlook. Talkeetna Roadhouse runs year-round, but check whether breakfast is open to non-guests. Groomed Nordic and fat-bike trails. Darker skies for aurora. Parks Hwy can be icy and dark, so 4.5 h round trip by car or overnight via the Aurora train.

name: Talkeetna Air Taxi 'Winter Explorer' Denali flightseeing
hoursOrDates: 1 Oct - 30 Apr, winter departure at noon, weather dependent. Office 9am-3pm daily.
cost: $325 adult (1 h); $475 with glacier landing (+$15 NPS fee)
notes: The best way to see Denali up close. Very weather-dependent, with a full refund if weather cancels. Two-person minimum. Short daylight means a single midday slot, so build in a spare day.

name: Snowhook Adventures dog sled ride
hoursOrDates: Oct-Apr (snow dependent), daily 10am, 12pm, 2pm, 4pm, plus a moonlit tour. Holiday dates ?
notes: Ride behind Iditarod-style teams on Willow trails near the Iditarod restart area. Gear is included. Dog-sled + ice-fishing combo runs Dec-Apr. Early-season trail conditions depend on snow. Shuttles from Anchorage need 24 h notice.

name: Fat-bike rental (Downtown Bicycle Rental)
hoursOrDates: Open daily year-round, ~10am-6pm. Holiday hours ?
cost: Studded fat bike $30 per 4 h weekday, $35 weekend; 24 h $45-55; e-fat $45-50 per 4 h
notes: Studded fat bikes straight onto the Tony Knowles Coastal Trail and Anchorage's ~130 mi of winter trails. Stay off groomed classic ski tracks. Text ahead to reserve for 6. Pogies are $5 and worth it.

name: Glacier City Snowmobile Tours
hoursOrDates: Winter. In early season (mid-Nov to Jan) it runs the Scenic Mountain tour (Crow Pass area/Iditarod Trail). Spencer/Blue Ice glacier tours are generally later in the season, subject to USFS permits.
cost: ? (expect ~$250-450 pp; +$12 USFS fee on USFS land)
notes: Guided backcountry riding with heated grips, gear and fire-pit lunch. Pickups in Girdwood. Snow-dependent in late Dec. Drivers usually need to be 16+ with licence, and there are combined weight limits for two-up. Alternatives: Alaska Wild Guides and Alaska Backcountry Access.

name: Guided ice fishing (Fishtale River Guides)
hoursOrDates: Once ice is safe, usually by late Nov / early Dec. Refund if ice is judged unsafe.
cost: $80 pp per 4 h + AK non-resident fishing licence (~$15-30)
notes: Gear is included, targeting trout and char on stocked lakes. Low-key and social. Alternatives with heated shelters and snowmachine transport: DeadStick (Wasilla) and Snowhook's sled + fishing combo. Bring a licence (buy online at ADF&G).

name: Anchorage Museum
hoursOrDates: Winter: Tue-Sat 10am-6pm, Sun 12-6pm, closed Mon (so closed 28 Dec). 25 Dec and 1 Jan probably closed (third-party listing). 24 and 31 Dec open? / maybe early close. Holidays are not on the official site, so call 907-929-9200.
notes: Alaska's best museum: Smithsonian Arctic Studies Center Native collections, art and history, plus a planetarium. Ideal for the dark afternoons. Holiday light displays on the lawn.

name: Alaska Native Heritage Center
hoursOrDates: Winter season (14 Sep 2026 - 8 May 2027): Mon-Fri 9am-5pm, closed weekends (26-27 Dec, 2-3 Jan). CLOSED 24 and 25 Dec. 31 Dec / 1 Jan not listed as closures, so call to confirm (907-330-8000). In the window it is open 23, 28, 29, 30 Dec, with 31 Dec and 1 Jan uncertain.
notes: Learn about Alaska's major Native cultures through exhibits and a gallery. Winter is self-guided only: outdoor village sites under snow, café closed, fewer live performances.

name: Anchorage New Year's Eve celebration & fireworks
coordNote: approx: Chinook lot, 3rd Ave & E St
hoursOrDates: 31 Dec. The 2025 pattern was 7-9pm with fireworks at 8pm (early, kid-friendly). The 2026 date and time are not yet confirmed.
notes: Run by the Anchorage Downtown Partnership: live music, food trucks, hot-toddy garden and sledding. The venue moved from Town Square to the Chinook lot in 2025. Eagle River also does fireworks at Lions Park. Dress for long standing in the cold.

name: Alyeska NYE Torchlight Parade & Fireworks
hoursOrDates: 31 Dec. 2025 pattern: parade ~9pm, fireworks ~9:30pm. Mountain closes 5pm that day.
notes: Skiers carry torches down the mountain, followed by fireworks. Watch from outside the Day Lodge. Live music at the Sitzmark. Driving back to Anchorage late on NYE along the Seward Hwy is dark and risky, so stay in Girdwood or pick a designated driver.

name: Town Square Park holiday tree & downtown lights
hoursOrDates: Tree lit from late Nov through the holiday season. Heyi Days winter promotion runs to 31 Dec.
notes: Big lit tree and light-wrapped downtown trees. Best enjoyed on an evening stroll with the Anchorage Museum lawn lights. Sidewalks can be icy.

name: Zoo Lights at the Alaska Zoo
hoursOrDates: 2026 dates TBC. Last season ran nightly 19 Dec - 4 Jan, 5-8pm, closed 25 Dec. Zoo daytime 10am-4pm, open 1 Jan, closed 25 Dec.
notes: Illuminated walking loop through the zoo, with daytime animals such as snow leopards, musk ox and moose. Buy tickets online in advance.

name: Brighter Winter Nights, Alaska Botanical Garden
hoursOrDates: Select evenings 3 Dec 2026 - 31 Jan 2027, 5-8pm (last entry 7:30). Holiday nights ?
notes: Light displays in a forest garden with glowing greenhouses, a fire pit and kicksled rides. Buy only via alaskabg.org because of scam ticket sites.

name: Snow City Cafe
hoursOrDates: Breakfast/lunch daily. Holiday hours ?
notes: Anchorage's favourite brunch (crab cakes Benedict, reindeer sausage). Long weekend waits, so join the waitlist or go early.

name: Moose's Tooth Pub & Pizzeria
hoursOrDates: Daily lunch-late. 25 Dec likely closed ?
notes: Legendary pizza and Broken Tooth beers. Always busy with waits of 30-60 min, so a group of 6 should go off-peak.

name: Spenard Roadhouse
hoursOrDates: Brunch/lunch/dinner. Holiday hours ?
notes: Comfort food, bacon-of-the-month and a good bar. Reservations help for 6.

name: Kriner's Diner
hoursOrDates: Breakfast/lunch. Holiday hours ?
notes: Huge diner breakfasts and sourdough pancakes, useful for carb-loading before a day out.

name: Fire Island Rustic Bakeshop
coordNote: Airport Heights location; there is also a South Addition shop near downtown
hoursOrDates: Mornings to early afternoon, closed some weekdays ?
notes: Excellent bread, pastries and coffee. Sells out early.

name: Kaladi Brothers Coffee
hoursOrDates: Daily
notes: Local roaster chain, with cafes everywhere. Easy pre-trailhead stop.

name: Midnight Sun Brewing
hoursOrDates: Afternoon-evening. Holiday hours ?
notes: Long-running craft brewery with a food menu, on the way back from Turnagain Arm.

name: Anchorage Brewing Company
hoursOrDates: Afternoon-evening. Holiday hours ?
notes: World-class barrel-aged and wild ales in a taproom with a pizza kitchen.

name: 49th State Brewing (downtown)
hoursOrDates: Daily lunch-late. Holiday hours ?
notes: Large brewpub with a rooftop view of Cook Inlet and good for groups. Reserve for 6, especially around NYE.

name: Simon & Seafort's
hoursOrDates: Dinner nightly, lunch weekdays. Holiday hours ?
notes: Classic Alaska seafood with Cook Inlet sunset views. Since sunset is ~15:45, book an early slot to see it.
